x: The AMASR (Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains) Act is of 1958. B is wrong: the Antiquities and Art Treasures Act is of 1972. C and D are wrong: ICOMOS was founded in 1965 (headquartered in Paris, not New Delhi) and evaluates cultural, not natural, World Heritage nominations.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Section 63 of the GoI Act 1935 let the Governor address the provincial legislature, and ministries drafted the speech from April 1937. Statement 3 is wrong: Article 175 provides for the address, but it is not mandatory. So 1 and 2 only.

Annapurna Studios (Akkineni Nageswara Rao, 1970s) is in Hyderabad. A and B are wrong: Ramanaidu Studios and Ramoji Film City are also in Hyderabad, not Madras. D is wrong: Vijaya Vauhini Studios was in Madras.

Adivi Bapiraju was a painter, poet and novelist (Narayana Rao, Himabindu). B is wrong: Vaddadi Papaiah illustrated magazine covers (Chandamama, Yuva); Bapu was the film director known for epic line drawings. C is wrong: Himabindu is Bapiraju's. D is wrong: the Rajahmundry pioneer of modern Andhra painting was Damerla Rama Rao.

Warli art belongs to Maharashtra. B is wrong: Pithora is the art of the Rathwa of Gujarat-MP, not Andhra Pradesh. C is wrong: Gond art belongs to Madhya Pradesh. D is wrong: Bhil art is not a Telangana-only form.

The State's tools against regionalism listed in the notes are the National Integration Council, Article 44, Article 51A and the Fifth, Sixth and Eighth Schedules. Article 32 (right to constitutional remedies) is not among them, so C is the answer.
